page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Compute resources are configured with 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 dedicated physical cores via simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Cache allocation comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory resources total 32.0 GB of RAM, corresponding to an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The instance features a substantial bundled local storage capacity of 2,880 GB on high-performance NVMe SSDs. Accelerated graphics hardware is absent, with a GPU count of zero.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core compute performance alongside average multi-core metrics. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 2,071.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3,078.28, both ranking in the top 25%. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) and standard cryptographic instructions (AES, VAES, SHA_NI), contributing to an average PassMark CPU encryption score of 4,812.91. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput sits in the middle 50%, with a PassMark CPU score of 7,524.08 and Geekbench multi-core score of 4,736.0.

Data throughput metrics present specific performance tradeoffs. While Redis SET operations maintain a solid pace of 6.17 million operations per second, memory bandwidth tests demonstrate lower relative efficiency, measuring 36.73 GB/sec on large-block read-only transfers and 303.46 GB/sec on cached small-block reads. Decompression and compilation benchmarks also show constraints, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 27.17 GB/sec and Clang software compilation scoring 5,420.0, both landing in the lower quartile. In language model inference, small 135M models generate 151.76 tokens/sec, but larger 7B models drop significantly to 7.69 tokens/sec due to limited core count and lack of hardware accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L4aos_v4 provides dense local NVMe storage relative to its 4 vCPU baseline, making it economical for I/O-intensive workloads without paying for excess compute cores. It fits transactional databases, intermediate data caching, log processing, and low-latency storage-heavy operations, though it is less suited for massive parallel compilation or large-model machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V, equipped with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The hardware layout features 4 vCPUs spanning 2 dedicated physical cores with multithreading, alongside 32.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per core) and 32 MB of L3 cache. Storage is a defining highlight, bundling 2,880 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity, while omitting dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile single-core metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2,071.0 and strong text processing, whereas multi-core compute and uncached memory bandwidth align within average to lower brackets. The server achieves 6.17 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, confirming its efficiency for storage-bound applications. The L4aos_v4 is suitable for high-throughput NoSQL engines, transactional databases, and localized data caching where substantial NVMe capacity takes precedence over heavy parallel processing.
